your_book:
Friday's session was broadly constructive for Jaleel's book, with the portfolio sitting at $23,123 and a modest $247 in unrealized gains (+1.08%). The clearest winners were NVIDIA (+2.93%, now +9.4% on the position) and the software cluster — NOW (+1.05%), ADBE (+1.01%), and SAP (+1.51%) — all riding a rotation narrative out of hardware and into less capital-intensive software names ahead of Microsoft's earnings. ZTS (+1.66%) and BSX (+1.59%) also had solid days despite both carrying elevated guidance-cut flags. The drag came from NVS (-1.45%), EFX (-1.99%), and KO (-1.02%), though none are large enough positions to meaningfully hurt the day.

The sharpest divergence to flag is NBIX (Neurocrine Biosciences), which collapsed -10.08% on Friday — an outsized single-day move that demands explanation before the next session. The system rates it STRONG BUY with a QARP of 76.2, but price and thesis are visibly separating. RKLB remains the book's thorniest structural problem: it's the largest single position at 14% of the portfolio ($3,247), carries a -17.1% loss, and is rated AVOID — meaning Jaleel is overweight a name the model explicitly doesn't endorse. That gap has not closed.

LULU (-0.51%, -7.0% on position) continues its slow bleed under a guidance-cut flag with Americas comps down five straight quarters; Michael Burry reportedly adding is a contrarian data point worth noting, but it doesn't change the fundamental picture. SPGI slipped -0.74% and is now -4.4% on the position with next read not until later in the cycle. The pharma cluster — GILD, NVS, VRTX, NBIX — faces a drug-pricing policy overhang with a key date of August 4, just days away. Watch that closely heading into next week.

attention.note: The MFN pricing overhang flag matures in days; with NBIX already down hard on Friday, the cluster needs monitoring heading into the weekend and the August 4 catalyst.
